stemMd: A laboratory rule says: “If a batch fails the sterility check, it is discarded.” A batch was discarded. What can be concluded from this rule alone?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The batch may or may not have failed the sterility check.

options.label: B
options.textMd: No batch that passes can ever be discarded.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It certainly failed the sterility check.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It certainly passed the sterility check.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The rule must have been broken.

explanationMd: The rule gives one sufficient cause of discarding, not the only possible cause. Observing the outcome therefore does not identify whether that cause occurred. A batch might have been discarded for failed sterility or for some other reason.

distractorRationale.c: This affirms the consequent; other reasons for discarding may exist.
distractorRationale.d: Discarding does not establish a pass either.
distractorRationale.b: The rule does not prohibit other causes of discarding.
distractorRationale.e: Discarding is compatible with the rule.
